body:
Metricool: scheduled Sun 2026-10-25 13:00 IG + TikTok
2 Vercel settings before your bill grows: drop Turbo builds, add an Ignored Build Step. CTA: VERCEL.
guide: This cuts your Vercel bill by lowering the build machine size and stopping every GitHub push from triggering a build. You need a Vercel account with a project connected to a GitHub repository.
1. Open the Vercel dashboard, go to Usage and look at build minutes per project to find which projects spend the most.
1. Open that project's Settings, go to the build and deployment section and find the build machine setting.
1. Change the build machine from the fastest option (turbo) to the lowest one if you can wait a little longer for each deploy.
1. Decide which pushes deserve a build, for example only the main branch, or only commits that change the app itself rather than notes or docs.
1. Add that rule to the project with Vercel's Ignored Build Step, a short script or command that tells Vercel to skip the build when a push doesn't need one.
1. Push a small change on a branch you excluded and check that Vercel skips the deployment.
1. Push a real change to the branch you kept and check that it still builds and deploys.
1. Look at build minutes again after a week or two to confirm the numbers have dropped.
Watch out: the fastest build machine is the default on new projects and the minutes add up quickly, so check both settings when you first create a site, not after a surprise bill.
